title: Plant Materials Ii
description: Identification, taxonomy, habits of growth, and cultural and environmental requirements of plants grown in California. Emphasis on the identification, use, and maintenance of plants commonly used in the landscaping and gardening industry. Plants are observed on campus and at off-site locations. This is the second of two plant courses covering the master plant list.
outcomes: Compare and contrast shrub features and cultural need.
Identify shrubs presented by botanical and common names.
objectives: List the botanical and common names, appearance, culture, adaptation, and use of California trees, shrubs, ground covers, vines, perennials, annuals, and interior plants, selected by faculty from program master list
Correctly identify all listed plants presented by botanical and common names
Design landscapes based on plant features, uses, and cultural needs in different landscape and garden applications and select plants that conform to specific landscape needs
Define horticultural and botanical terms and use them to identify plant parts and characteristics
Describe the importance of soil and ecology of different plants
Describe the binomial nomenclature utilized in the identification plants
Describe plant growth habits and requirements
Recognize the variety of ways plants are utilized by different cultures around the world
Use a computer program to select plants for various landscape and garden situations
content: List plants selected for the class by name, appearance, use, culture, and adaption, including:
By genus, species, and, if applicable, variety or cultivar
Design landscapes in landscape and garden applications by:
Plant form, color, texture, and line
Plants to address specific landscape needs
Define terms used to identify plant parts and characteristics, including:
Describe soil and ecological conditions for plants
Native plants to bay area region
Describe binomial nomenclature and its use for identification of plants
Identify plant growth and habits and requirements
Describe the cultural uses of plants
Identify plants using various ID keys
Develop a key for personal use
Use computer software to select plants for various uses
